name: Carbocisteine
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Carbocisteine is a mucolytic. The Irish label gives no kidney or dialysis dosing and no pharmacokinetic data on kidney impairment, so no evidence-based adjustment can be stated. Its main safety issue is gastrointestinal bleeding in people with ulcer history. It has no US FDA label.
kidney_function_basis: The SmPC does not address kidney impairment; bands are shown on creatinine clearance (CrCl) for consistency.

bands.recommendation: Usual dose: 2,250 mg/day in divided doses (two 375 mg capsules three times daily), reduced to 1,500 mg/day (one capsule four times daily) once response is achieved (SmPC).
The SmPC gives no kidney dosing and no kidney pharmacokinetic data. Use with caution and specialist judgment.

monitoring: Gastrointestinal bleeding, especially in older adults, ulcer history or with drugs that cause bleeding; stop if bleeding occurs (SmPC 4.4).
